title: Cascade Handoff: Simplify console navigation and workspace switching
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Console users (engineers, platform teams, and product owners) report friction when switching contexts, finding rollout dashboards, and getting a clear cost breakdown for a given model/route. The current sidebar is deep and role-agnostic which leads to hidden features, accidental navigations, and long task flows when triaging performance or costs.

Goal: Deliver an information architecture and primary navigation pattern that: 1) reduces workspace switch time, 2) surfaces per-route rollouts and cost lenses without additional clicks, 3) scales across Hosted/Dedicated/Private product modes, and 4) remains keyboard-friendly for power users.

Scope: Console top-level nav, left rail (compact + expanded states), global workspace switcher, contextual command palette, and the header cost-rollout quickstrip. Includes mid-fidelity interactive prototype and a small moderated usability test. Excludes detailed per-dashboard UI copy and final accessibility polishing (follow-up tickets).

Success metrics: median workspace-switch time < 3s in 90% of test flows; reduce average clicks to reach rollout panel from 4 -> 1; positive first-click success in usability testing >= 85%.
comments: 2026-01-30 - Aisha Khan: Kickoff + stakeholder alignment. Collected pain points from Growth, SRE, and a dedicated-customer panel (notes in Confluence).

2026-02-07 - Camila Ortiz: Delivered three divergent sketches: 'compact-rail', 'split-rail + header strip', and 'modal-quick-jump'. Team prefers split-rail for discoverability. Refer to /design-files for sketches.

2026-02-18 - Daniel Park (Eng): Flagged constraints around multi-tenant breadcrumb state and telemetry hooks. Suggested incremental API to fetch 'workspace lenses' to avoid a full navigation refactor.

2026-02-24 - Usability test: 8 participants (3 PMs, 3 engineers, 2 SREs). Quick-jump modal had fastest time but lower discoverability; split-rail had best discoverability but required compact state optimization. Full notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/console-ia/cascade-handoff/usability-notes

2026-03-03 - Camila Ortiz: Mid-fidelity prototype completed. PRD updated with final IA and interaction spec. Figma link added to design_files. Waiting on design review slot with product on 2026-03-09.

2026-03-10 - Ben Russo (PM): Reviewed and asked for clearer affordance for 'cost lens' and a persistent tokenized view when switching workspaces. Added PM-772 as follow-up for rollout communication copy.
2026-03-12 - Design review: Approved with minor changes. Action: handoff to Eng via ENG-41112 and schedule small pilot release behind feature flag.
decisions: Adopt 'Split-rail + Header Quickstrip' as the primary pattern: a compact left rail that expands on hover or via keyboard, plus a persistent header strip that surfaces 'Cost' and 'Rollouts' for the active workspace.
Include a modal command palette (Ctrl+K) as the power-user path for jumping across workspaces and routes. This will handle edge cases where users prefer a keyboard-first workflow.
Progressive rollout behind a feature flag per org; default to old nav for 10% of orgs during pilot to gather telemetry and error rates.
Design will supply a lightweight localization-ready copy deck, Eng to own implementation of telemetry events defined in the PRD.
next_steps: Handoff package to Eng (ENG-41112): include interaction specs, aria roles, and tokenized cost-strip component.
Create implementation tickets for compact state animation and KV-cache for workspace meta fetch: ENG-41113, ENG-41114.
PM to schedule pilot cohort and update release notes (PM-772).
Design follow-ups: DES-902469 - iconography and microcopy for quickstrip; DES-902470 - accessibility pass and color-contrast checks.
Run A/B telemetry: measure workspace switch time and clicks to rollout across pilot orgs for 2 weeks post-launch.
review_feedback: Ben Russo (PM): Ensure the cost quickstrip communicates estimated per-token and per-minute cost; include link to breakdown modal.
Daniel Park (Eng): Prefer incremental API that returns workspace 'lenses' to prevent a heavy nav boot-time cost. Validate on Dedicated clusters first.
Evelyn Zhou (Security): Confirm that the workspace switch does not expose resources across org boundaries; suggested adding an audit event on switch.
Usability lead: Reduce animation duration to 100ms for compact-rail expand to preserve perceived performance.
